title: VPC allocator & routing orchestrator Terraform module with canary upgrades and health probes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a reusable Terraform module (and accompanying test harness) that provisions a VPC networking stack optimized for Redwood Private deployments. Module responsibilities: automated subnet allocation patterns (control/compute/ingress/egress), NAT gateway and IGW wiring, VPC Endpoint (interface and gateway) templates, route table attachments, cross-AZ routing policies, and a reconciliation-driven controller for safe, automated upgrades.

Goals:
- Provide a single module that can be composed into customer stacks (on-prem and VPC) with clear knobs for AZ topology, subnet sizing, and egress patterns.
- Implement safe upgrade hooks: canary rollout of route changes and endpoint replacements with automatic rollback on health regressions.
- Expose synthetic health probes and passive metrics (endpoint reachability, NAT throughput, route convergence) to Console/observability.
- Support deterministic naming and tagging for audit logs and KMS identity mapping.

Non-goals:
- This module does not manage tenant-level firewall rules or application security groups beyond tag-based attachments.
- It will not replace higher-level service discovery; focus is on infra primitives and safe orchestration.

Approach and design decisions:
- Subnet allocator: implement deterministic CIDR splitting with zone-aware sizing; allow opt-out for static CIDRs. Offer a "density_hint" parameter to recommend /20-/24 ranges depending on expected compute scale.
- Egress fabric: prefer NAT gateway autoscaling pattern (multiple small NGWs per AZ) behind an orchestrator to reduce single-NAT failure blast radius. Provide IGW fallback for low-cost dev tiers.
- VPC endpoints: generate interface endpoints for control-plane services and gateway endpoints for S3/Dynamo; support policy templates and endpoint-specific route table attachments.
- Routing templates: route tables modeled as modular resources with table-per-subnet default and explicit attach/detach APIs to support canary routing changes.
- Upgrade strategy: use a reconciliation loop that applies changes to a single AZ/subnet (canary) and runs a set of probes; only promote to remaining AZs after passing SLAs. Rollback via Terraform plan/apply reversal and temporary route shadowing when necessary.
- Health checks: implement both synthetic probes (e.g., curl to endpoint IPs via VPC endpoints, STS health calls) and passive observability (flow logs sampling, NAT error counters). Expose probe results as tags on resources and as metrics for Console ingestion.

Compatibility and constraints:
- Targeted Terraform versions: 1.5+ (keep HCL2 compatible). Use provider pinning for aws provider to avoid subtle drift.
- Must be usable in air-gapped on-prem setups: avoid external provider data sources unless explicitly enabled.

Deliverables:
- terraform/modules/vpc-orchestrator (module code + examples)
- test-harness/terraform/integration (acct-level tests that exercise canary upgrades)
- Confluence design doc and runbook for on-call + upgrade procedure
- Console dashboard template for module telemetry

Operational acceptance criteria are below.
acceptance_criteria:
- Module exposes inputs for AZ list, subnet sizing, egress mode (nat-per-az|shared-nat|igw-only), and endpoint list.
- Integration example successfully applies in staging and creates expected subnets, NATs, endpoints, and route tables.
- Canary upgrade flow: modify route table in staging canary AZ, run probes, verify promotion to remaining AZs only after probes pass.
- Health probes emit metrics to Console and an example dashboard shows endpoint reachability, NAT error rate, and route convergence time.
- Module passes security review (IAM least privilege for endpoints and NGWs) and audit tags are present on all resources.
- Terraform plan/apply idempotency for repeated runs with identical inputs.
- Test harness includes automated rollback scenario that demonstrates safe reversal within target RTO (15 minutes).
